why_agent_can_change_it: All three traces show the agent choosing to act/assume instead of asking one clarifying question when the request was under-specified: trace 1 assumed which store/product the shopper meant instead of confirming it, trace 2 assumed an order id instead of asking the customer to confirm it, and trace 3 ran ~30 speculative searches after zero matches and then asserted an unsupported 'we can often find the right style keywords' instead of stating nothing matched or asking for more detail. This is a decision-procedure failure (when to ask vs. when to act/search), not a missing capability or data gap, so it is addressable directly: a prompt rule requiring a tool-actionable clarifying question before any write action or further speculative search on ambiguous input, a harness check that blocks a write tool call until an identifying parameter has been confirmed, or a tightened tool description that stops the agent from asking for unusable identifiers (e.g. a product link).
